Flood fill (洪水填充): starting from a cell, visit every connected cell of the same kind (BFS or DFS) and mark it. Counting how many times a new fill has to start counts the connected regions. "Connected" must be defined: 4 neighbours (edges) or 8 neighbours (edges and corners).

Mark cells when they are pushed, not when they are popped, or a cell can enter the queue many times. On large grids prefer BFS or an explicit stack over recursion, which can overflow on a 1000 × 1000 region.

Lake Counting (P1596) uses 8-connectivity. Overwriting the grid itself is the cheapest "visited" mark when the grid is not needed afterwards.
Two frontiers; expand the smaller layer.

Bidirectional BFS (双向广搜): when the start and the goal are both known, search from both ends at once and stop when the two frontiers meet. If each state has b neighbours and the answer is d, one BFS visits about bd states, two half-searches about 2·bd/2: the square root.

Expand the smaller frontier each round, one whole layer at a time; when a newly reached state is already known from the other side, answer = its distance from this side + its distance from the other side. The moves must be reversible (or searched backwards with reversed moves).

The 8-puzzle (八数码难题 P1379) again (A* in 进阶篇第4章). Each sliding move is its own reverse, so the backward search uses the same moves. Finishing whole layers keeps the meeting distance correct.
Deepening on g + h; search summary.

IDA* = iterative deepening (进阶篇第4章) + an A* estimate h. Search depth-first with a bound D on g + h: cut any branch where moves so far + the estimate of moves still needed > D. If the search fails, raise D.
Memory is just the recursion stack, and a good h cuts most of the tree.

h must never overestimate (as in A*). For sliding or swapping puzzles, "number of misplaced pieces" (or that number divided by what one move can fix) is the usual choice. Also skip the move that undoes the previous one.
